text:
Samir: Customer (AcmeAnalytics) — their embedded analytics widget keeps prompting for MFA/reauth every ~10-15m after we rotated the org API key. Happens in Chrome/Edge, not Safari. Logs show 'reauth_required'. Anyone seen this pattern?

Asha: Quick guess — cookie/SameSite or third-party cookie blocking. @Maya can you pull the session refresh traces for org-acme? :thinking:

Maya: Looking at the traces now. Repeated POST /auth/refresh returning 401 with reason 'nonce_mismatch' and a new Set-Cookie each time. It looks like the refresh flow is trying to set a cross-site cookie from the iframe and the browser is ignoring it. Snippet:```
2026-03-17T12:31:02Z POST /auth/refresh 401 nonce_mismatch org=acme
Set-Cookie: rw_sess=eyJ...; SameSite=None; Secure; Path=/; Domain=redwood.com
```

Samir: The widget is embedded at app.acme.com (iframe src=https://dash.redwood.com/embed/...). Cookie domain is redwood.com. Customer says they did a key rotation via the org console right before this started.

Asha: If third-party cookies are blocked, the browser will ignore Set-Cookie from the iframe and the session never persists. We rely on a silent postMessage fallback that exchanges a short-lived nonce, but after the rotation the handshake stores the nonce on the top-level cookie instead of the iframe storage — so the iframe can't access it. :grimacing:

Maya: Repro steps I used (Chrome stable, default 3rd-party cookies blocked):
1) Open incognito, go to customer page (app.acme.com)
2) Load widget iframe -> network shows POST /auth/silent -> server replies with Set-Cookie SameSite=None
3) Browser console: "Cookie blocked: Third-party cookie"
4) Widget shows reauth modal, and subsequent refresh attempts keep getting 401s.

Samir: Customer can toggle "Block third-party cookies" off and it works, but that's not acceptable to them. Is there a server-side fallback we can enable quickly?

Asha: Options:
- Implement a top-level redirect reauth (open a new tab) — reliable but UX regression.
- Use an explicit user-consent popup to allow cross-site cookie for the session (not ideal).
- Enhance postMessage fallback to include a signed nonce delivered by the top-level app when the iframe initially loads — requires SDK change and security review.
- Add a short grace window for token rotation so existing nonces remain valid for ~5 minutes after key rotate (low-effort mitigation).
Note: Passing session tokens in URL/query is a hard no for security.

OpsBot: Created ticket RW-7182 and escalated to Security & SDK teams. https://redwood.atlassian/issue/RW-7182 :rotating_light:

Maya: I uploaded a minimal repro (network HAR + steps) to the ticket and a tiny gist with the iframe sandbox: https://gist.github.com/redwood/repro-iframe-3p-cookie. Attaching network dump there.

Asha: For immediate mitigation, request the customer to postpone the key rotation while we deploy a 5-minute rotation-grace and increase logging to capture device_fingerprint and client_user_agent for failed refreshes. @security-team please weigh in on the rotation-grace risk.

Samir: Messaging customer now: "We're investigating — short-term options: delay further key rotations for your org or use the top-level reauth flow. We expect a mitigation within 24 hours." :thumbsup: 

Maya: Follow-up: I can add a temporary flag on staging to enable the rotation-grace and run a canary for a subset of orgs to validate. Will post results to RW-7182.

Asha: Thanks team. We'll keep CS updated and loop in the SDK owners for a longer-term postMessage/handshake fix.
